title: Default-key OutGuess does not separate an LP2 page
claim: Across the declared 75 canonical carriers, the frozen default-key OutGuess 0.13 test recognized all ten known LP1 positive controls but no LP2 page separated from the repeated FFFFFFFF false-header distribution or its page-specific matched null.
why_it_matters: It converts visually persuasive complete LP2 extractions into a controlled branch closure, preventing capacity-bound artifacts from being reused as payload evidence.
controls: Ten known LP1 positive carriers, including held-out Page 08.
Independent retrieval agreement on all 75 pages.
Page-specific matched nulls and familywise correction across 225 tests.
limitations: The claim is restricted to OutGuess 0.13 with the default-key path and the hashed canonical carriers.
Carrier JPEGs and coefficient bitmaps are not redistributed, so the public package verifies the complete retained ledgers rather than rerunning extraction from pixels.
Other keys, recompressions, crops, rotations, steganographic systems, and independently frozen methods are outside scope.
does_not_claim: That Liber Primus contains no steganography.
That every possible OutGuess key or carrier transformation has been tested.
Any LP2 plaintext, translation, cryptographic key, locator, endpoint, or complete solve.
That absence of a detector positive proves absence under methods outside the frozen test.
current_interpretation: Remove the tested default-key OutGuess extraction path from active LP2 key channels and retain it only as a regression and canonical-carrier provenance control.
